text:
Maria: Hey team, my docs PR #2078 preview on Netlify is serving a bunch of assets as 403. Netlify preview: https://app.netlify.com/sites/redwood-docs/deploys/12345 :confused:
Sam: :eyes: odd. Local `mkdocs serve` works for me. Can you paste the preview URL and one failing asset path?
Maria: preview URL above, failing asset example: /assets/sdk/python/main.js -> 403. The browser console shows `GET https://.../assets/sdk/python/main.js 403`
Jon: Can you grab the Netlify deploy log? sometimes the _headers or `_redirects` step clobbers things.
ci-bot: Netlify build succeeded (status: succeeded) — 2023-11-02T18:12:09Z. Artifacts uploaded: manifest.json, assets.tar.gz.
Rachel: If it uploaded gzipped assets, Netlify sometimes requires `Content-Encoding: gzip` metadata preserved. Did the CI un-tar and re-upload?
Maria: CI buildpack creates `assets.tar.gz` then `netlify deploy` step extracts. I see a line in the deploy log: `uploaded 412 files` and later `skipped 0 files`. No explicit headers step.
Sam: Could be a base_url mismatch too — if mkdocs config `site_url` or `use_directory_urls` changed the path. Are paths in the generated HTML pointing to `/assets/sdk/python/...` or `./assets/...`?
Maria: HTML references `/assets/sdk/python/main.js` (absolute). Locally that serves fine.
Alex: Two quick checks: 1) inspect object ACLs/headers in the Netlify deploy UI; 2) try toggling `--no-asset-transform` in the deploy step if we have a custom uploader.
Sam: Another possibility: we switched the SDK folder name from `sdk/python` to `client/python` in a rename, and CI still bundles old path but the CDN rewrote paths. Less likely but happened before.
Jon: Can you paste a short excerpt of the Netlify deploy log showing the assets portion?
Maria: pastebin: https://paste.redwood.ai/xyz (excerpt below)
```
Uploading assets.tar.gz... done
Extracting assets...
Uploading assets/...
uploaded assets/sdk/python/main.js (gzip)
uploaded assets/sdk/python/main.js.meta
Setting headers for gzipped assets
```

Jon: That `Setting headers for gzipped assets` line is interesting — do we actually set `Content-Encoding: gzip`? If we set metadata incorrectly Netlify might reject direct GETs with 403.
Rachel: Also check netlify.toml — if we have a `[[headers]]` block that denies access to certain paths for previews. Someone added a preview-only block a while back for `/private/` stuff.
Maria: grep shows nothing for `/assets` in netlify.toml.
Sam: Quick local workaround to reproduce: run the same extraction step and serve the static files with `python -m http.server` and request the file with `curl -I` to see headers.
Maria: Doing that now.
Alex: For a short-term fix, if it's a header metadata problem, republishing the assets with `Content-Encoding` set correctly usually fixes it. I can push a small CI step to reapply headers on deploy.
Sam: If Alex can push that, Maria, you can re-trigger the preview and we can validate.
Maria: I'll queue an extra commit to the PR with a small netlify deploy script tweak. Also: reviewers — @Sam and @Jon, can you please review quickly? We want to merge before the midnight docs sync window.
Sam: Happy to review once CI passes. If it's just the header script, feel free to merge after my approval. :thumbsup:
Jon: Same. Aim to merge before 23:50 PST. If CI flakes, ping me and we'll fast-track.
Maria: Local repro confirms missing `Content-Encoding: gzip` header when we rehost files via the CI extraction step. Adding a fix: in `scripts/deploy_assets.sh` add `aws s3 cp --content-encoding gzip ... --metadata-directive REPLACE` (we're using the s3-compatible upload). Pushing in 5m.
ci-bot: Build started for branch docs/2078 at 2023-11-02T18:19:02Z
Sam: Quick manual test instructions for anyone else: 1) `git checkout docs/2078` 2) `docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/site -w /site squidfunk/mkdocs-material mkdocs build -d /tmp/site` 3) `python -m http.server --directory /tmp/site 8000` 4) `curl -I http://localhost:8000/assets/sdk/python/main.js` — confirm `Content-Encoding: gzip` header is present
Rachel: Nice minimal repro. Could also use `mkdocs serve` but this replicates the build output exactly.
Maria: Pushed fix (commit 8a9f3c). CI ran the additional header step and netlify preview now returns 200 for that file. Preview link: https://app.netlify.com/sites/redwood-docs/deploys/12346
Sam: Checking preview... 200 and headers look good. :tada:
Jon: Approved on the PR.
Sam: Approved as well.
Maria: Thanks! I'll merge after the nightly docs merge window check — since it's not a content change, I'll merge immediately but hold off if anyone flags a release conflict.
Alex: FYI, I'll open a small follow-up to add a unit test for the deploy step so we don't regress headers in future.
Maria: Sounds good. Closing the loop here. :white_check_mark:
